receipt transactionHash: missing, another transaction's (with status 0x1, with 0x0, and with no status: the reviewer's case), malformed or null keep it pending; the same hash in capitals counts
receipt blockNumber: missing, null, "0x", "abc", a number, 0x0, or below the block the payment was sent at keep it pending; the send block itself and later count
receipt blockHash: missing, null, short, not hex, or without 0x keep it pending; a 32-byte hash counts
receipt identity: a from or to that contradicts the payment, or a missing from/to, keeps it pending; the same addresses in another case count

invalid receipts first (3 with no status / a bad block number, then 3 with another hash), each claiming the OPPOSITE status, then a valid one: only the valid one decides (confirmed for 0x1, reverted for 0x0)
the first reader answers a malformed receipt (another hash, status 0x0), the next reader a valid one (0x1): confirmed, in the same round, from the next reader
every reader answers a malformed receipt (another hash, no status) for good: never confirmed or reverted; "cannot confirm" at TRACK.lost, unknown at TRACK.stop, receipts asked until then
replacement: the receipt for the transaction that spent the nonce belongs to the original, to another tx, has no status, or another sender: no verdict; once valid: "replaced"

guard, the documented policy (one valid receipt from the reader asked, no cross-check, no reorg re-check): the first reader's valid 0x0 decides even if another reader says 0x1; a first reader that has no receipt yet keeps it pending
the page itself (WITNESS): the reviewer's receipt (another transaction's hash, no status) is never "reverted"; the payment stays pending, then a valid receipt confirms it

cases.name: a reader answers the original hash with ANOTHER transaction of the same sender (the one that spent nonce 7): not trusted, the next reader is asked; stays pending (never "replaced"), then its own receipt confirms
a reader answers the right hash but another sender: unusable, the next reader is asked (not the wallet first); the real nonce decides
the reader's answer has a missing or malformed hash (and nonce 7, pointing at the sender's other transaction): never used, the next reader is asked; pending, then confirmed
the reader's nonce is missing, negative or not a hex quantity: never used (no "replaced", no early "unknown"), the next reader is asked; a valid nonce 0x0 is used (cancelled at nonce 0)
the first reader is invalid, the second valid: the second reader's nonce decides (a real cancellation at nonce 7 is "cancelled"); the wallet is never asked
every public reader answers the original hash with another transaction: none trusted; the wallet is asked and its valid answer (nonce 8) keeps it pending; then confirmed

the readers have not seen it and the WALLET answers with another transaction (or another sender, a malformed nonce, another call, recipient, value or chain): not trusted, stays pending; asked at most 5 times; then confirmed
a poisoned nonce (another hash, nonce 7) where nonce 7 was spent by the same call / a cancellation / another call: never confirmed, cancelled or replaced; pending until its own receipt

legitimate speed-up, cancellation and replacement are still classified right, from the public readers alone, for every legitimate representation of the original (data/input, checksum, upper-case hash, no chainId, leading zero)
late original receipt after "unknown" (no reader and no wallet gives a usable transaction): unknown at TRACK.lost, then its own receipt still confirms
a replacement whose block, transaction and receipt contradict each other (block number, blockHash, tx hash) is no proof: pending while it lasts; replaced once consistent
end to end: WITNESS sent, the first reader answers its hash with the sender's other mined transaction (nonce 7): never "replaced"/"cancelled", then "confirmed" from its own receipt
